{{Short description|German biologist}}
{{Primary sources|date=August 2021}}
'''Carl-Philipp Heisenberg''' (born 1968) is a German developmental biologist specializing in [[embryology]], [[cell biology]], and [[biophysics]]. He is the grandson of the physicist [[Werner Heisenberg]] and nephew of biologist [[Martin Heisenberg]]. He was born in Munich, Germany.

After graduating in [[Biology]] in Munich in 1992, he carried out his PhD work with [[Christiane Nüsslein-Volhard]] in Tübingen in 1997.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Heisenberg |first1=C.P. |last2=Brand |first2=M. |last3=Jiang |first3=Y.J. |last4=Warga |first4=R.M. |last5=Beuchle |first5=D. |last6=van Eeden |first6=F.J. |last7=Furutani-Seiki |first7=M. |last8=Granato |first8=M. |last9=Haffter |first9=P. |last10=Hammerschmidt |first10=M. |last11=Kane |first11=D.A. |last12=Kelsh |first12=R.N. |last13=Mullins |first13=M.C. |last14=Odenthal |first14=J. |last15=Nusslein-Volhard |first15=C. |title=Genes involved in forebrain development in the zebrafish, Danio rerio |journal=Development |date=1 December 1996 |volume=123 |issue=1 |pages=191–203 |doi=10.1242/dev.123.1.191 |pmid=9007240 }}</ref> After a [[Postdoctoral researcher|postdoc]] with Stephen Wilson at [[University College London]],<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Heisenberg |first1=Carl-Philipp |last2=Tada |first2=Masazumi |last3=Rauch |first3=Gerd-Jörg |last4=Saúde |first4=Leonor |last5=Concha |first5=Miguel L. |last6=Geisler |first6=Robert |last7=Stemple |first7=Derek L. |last8=Smith |first8=James C. |last9=Wilson |first9=Stephen W. |title=Silberblick/Wnt11 mediates convergent extension movements during zebrafish gastrulation |journal=Nature |date=May 2000 |volume=405 |issue=6782 |pages=76–81 |doi=10.1038/35011068 |pmid=10811221 |bibcode=2000Natur.405...76H |s2cid=4397286 }}</ref> he started his research group in 2001 at the [[Max Planck Institute for Cell Biology and Genetics]] in Dresden as an [[Emmy Noether]] junior professor.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.mpi-cbg.de/research-groups/alumni/|title=MPI-CBG: Alumni|website=www.mpi-cbg.de|access-date=2021-07-14|archive-date=2016-08-05|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160805110504/http://www.mpi-cbg.de/research-groups/alumni/|url-status=dead}}</ref>
Since 2010, he is a professor at the [[Institute of Science and Technology Austria]].<ref name="Heisenberg Group">{{Cite web|url=https://ist.ac.at/en/research/heisenberg-group/|title=Heisenberg Group}}</ref>

Heisenberg was elected member of the [[German National Academy of Sciences Leopoldina]] in 2015<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.leopoldina.org/mitgliederverzeichnis/mitglieder/member/Member/show/ferdinand-hoff/|title=Mitglieder|website=Nationale Akademie der Wissenschaften Leopoldina}}</ref> and of the [[European Molecular Biology Organisation]] in 2016.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://people.embo.org/profile/carl-philipp-heisenberg|title=Find people in the EMBO Communities|website=people.embo.org}}</ref> In 2019, he received the [[Carus medal]] from the Leopoldina.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://ist.ac.at/en/news/carus-medal-awarded-to-ist-austria-professor-carl-philipp-heisenberg/|title=Carus Medal awarded to IST Austria professor Carl-Philipp Heisenberg}}</ref>

Heisenberg's research focuses on characterising the molecular, cellular and physical regulation of embryonic development.<ref name="Heisenberg Group"/> Using mostly [[zebrafish]] as a model organism, his group has identified how cytoskeletal and adhesive elements control the physical properties of tissues during [[gastrulation]].<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Krieg |first1=M. |last2=Arboleda-Estudillo |first2=Y. |last3=Puech |first3=P.-H. |last4=Käfer |first4=J. |last5=Graner |first5=F. |last6=Müller |first6=D.
